metadata.title: Breakthrough in Energy-Efficient Quantum Microelectronics with Redox Gating

text_resource.text:
April 14 is World Quantum Day, an annual event to celebrate how we use the science of atoms and particles—the building blocks of the universe—to advance science and technology.
Scientists and engineers already leverage the strange and interesting properties of quantum mechanics to advance our technology. Our understanding of quantum mechanics helps us design the semiconductors used in cars, phones, and other technology. GPS systems rely on the quantum mechanics of ultra-precise atomic clocks.
Many more advancements in quantum technology are yet to come. Secure communication through metropolitan-scale entangled quantum networks, quantum machine clusters for high-end computation, and quantum sensors that enhance intracellular sensing and mapping are just some of the predicted developments.
Learn more about the some of the latest quantum research and announcements coming from the UChicago Pritzker School of Molecular Engineering and its partners below.
**Scientists use novel technique to create new energy-efficient microelectronic device**
Researchers at UChicago Pritzker Molecular Engineering and Argonne National Laboratory have achieved a breakthrough that could allow for a new kind of microelectronic material to consume only a fraction of the electricity of conventional electronics while still operating at peak performance. In a new study published in , the Argonne team proposed a new kind of ​“redox gating” technique that can control the movement of electrons in and out of a semiconducting material.
**Researchers from startups, government labs, and academia develop new techniques for making qubits out of erbium**
Two research groups—one at quantum startup , founded by UChicago Pritzker Molecular Engineering alumnus Manish Singh, and one at the U.S. Department of Energy’s Argonne National Laboratory—have used different host materials for erbium to advance quantum technology, demonstrating the versatility of this kind of quantum bit (qubit) and highlighting the importance of materials science to quantum computing and quantum communication.
Researchers at UChicago Pritzker Molecular Engineering, including Chicago Quantum Exchange IBM postdoctoral scholar Junyu Liu, and collaborators show in a new paper how incorporating quantum computing into the classical machine learning process can potentially help make machine learning more sustainable and efficient.
**In novel quantum computer design, qubits use magnets to selectively communicate**
An international team of researchers have begun to use magnets to entangle qubits, the building blocks of quantum computers; the simple technique could unlock complex capabilities.
Researchers have developed a new computational tool to describe how the atoms within quantum materials behave when they absorb and emit light. The tool will be released as part of the open-source software package , developed within the (MICCoM).
**Researchers invent new way to stretch diamond for better quantum bits**
A team of UChicago Pritzker Molecular Engineering researchers announced a breakthrough in quantum network engineering: By “stretching” thin films of diamond, they created quantum bits that can operate with significantly reduced equipment and expense. The change also makes the bits easier to control. 
A team led by the U.S. Department of Energy’s (DOE) Argonne National Laboratory has achieved a major milestone toward future quantum computing. They have extended the coherence time for their novel type of qubit to an impressive 0.1 milliseconds—nearly a thousand times better than the previous record.

metadata.title: Vitamin D Deficiency: Causes, Effects, and Prevention

text_resource.text:
Vitamin D deficiency is a common vitamin deficiency that causes issues with your bones and muscles. It most commonly affects people over the age of 65 and people who have darker skin. It’s preventable and treatable.
Cleveland Clinic is a non-profit academic medical center. Advertising on our site helps support our mission. We do not endorse non-Cleveland Clinic products or services. 
Vitamin D deficiency means you don’t have enough vitamin D in your body. It primarily causes issues with your bones and .
Cleveland Clinic is a non-profit academic medical center. Advertising on our site helps support our mission. We do not endorse non-Cleveland Clinic products or services. 
Vitamin D is an essential vitamin that your body uses for normal bone development and maintenance. Vitamin D also plays a role in your , and .
You can get vitamin D in a variety of ways, including:
  * Sun exposure on your skin (however, people with darker skin and older people may not get enough vitamin D through sunlight. Your geographical location may also prevent adequate vitamin D exposure through sunlight).


Despite all these methods to get vitamin D, vitamin D deficiency is a common worldwide problem.
Vitamin D is one of many vitamins your body needs to stay healthy. It plays a crucial role in maintaining the balance of and bones and in building and maintaining bones.
More specifically, you need vitamin D so your body can use calcium and phosphorus to build bones and support healthy tissues.
With chronic and/or severe vitamin D deficiency, a decline in calcium and phosphorus absorption by your intestines leads to (low calcium levels in your blood). This leads to secondary (overactive parathyroid glands attempting to keep blood calcium levels normal).
Both hypocalcemia and hyperparathyroidism, if severe, can cause symptoms, including muscle weakness and cramps, fatigue and depression.
To try to balance calcium levels in your blood (via secondary hyperparathyroidism), your body takes calcium from your bones, which leads to accelerated bone demineralization (when a bone breaks down faster than it can reform).
This can further result in (soft bones) in adults and in children.
Osteomalacia and osteoporosis put you at an increased risk for . Rickets is the same as osteomalacia, but it only affects children. Since a child’s bones are still growing, demineralization causes bowed or bent bones.
Anyone can have vitamin D deficiency, including infants, children and adults.
Vitamin D deficiency may be more common in people with higher skin content (darker skin) and who wear clothing with extensive skin coverage, particularly in Middle Eastern countries.
Vitamin D deficiency is a common global issue. About 1 billion people worldwide have vitamin D deficiency, while 50% of the population has vitamin D insufficiency.
Approximately 35% of adults in the United States have vitamin D deficiency.

However, you may have no signs or symptoms of vitamin D deficiency.

  * Not getting enough vitamin D in your diet and/or through sunlight.

metadata.title: Can't Use 10 Rare Cat Tickets for Guaranteed Event in Battle Cats

text_resource.text:
Weirdly cute cats run rampant across the galaxy! Here's your chance to raise and play with them for free! 
So, saved my Rare Cat Tickets, and just got the 10th one; figured I'd drop them and get one of the Xmas Galaxies... To see that instead of the tickets, its got the 1500 catfood listed on the guaranteed button. Are you unable to use 10 Rare Tickets instead of 1500? (i.e., is there no reason to save them up instead?) 
(Note- I have over 1500 Cat Food- does it just mean catfood goes first or can you not ever use 10 rare cat tickets to get the 10x bonuses associated with the current Rare Ticket banner...?) 
We made one of the first open-source MMORPG's with BitCraft Online. Join the vibrant community in one single shared world and Wishlist Now on Steam!
You can't use 10 Rare Tickets to spin the guaranteed. 
I thought it was only for guarenteed but it actually does for any kind of event in BCEN so it isn't possible to roll 10 rare tickets in one time. 
I like to save rare tickets up anyway for when there are triple chances for what I want lol 
Yeah, you can't use your own 10 rare tickets. You HAVE to spend the 1500 catfood. I was also upset by this when I found out. If you're patient enough to save up TEN rare tickets, they should allow you to benefit from the guaranteed events with them. ffs. 
The good news is, you using up those 10 rare tickets is just getting you closer to the eventual inevitable uber rare that you'll someday get from a regular rare ticket. Each player as a set-list of rare cats they are going to have. It never changes no matter what. So yeah, you might be guaranteed to get 40 regular rare cats. But you're also guaranteed to get an uber at point. 
I guess that's something... But I have to second the FFS. 
Wish I knew how long until the next Guaranteed roll; could use another anti-alien, but not sure I want to burn 1500 for Ubers that aren't top tier. 
> Each player as a set-list of rare cats they are going to have. It never changes no matter what. 
Actually, guaranteed uber rolls change the track. We know this because people who save scum noticed their upcoming cats would change after doing a guarenteed uber. 
I usually save up my tickets to use during the triple chance for ubers events; not sure if it actually works though 
theres no way 2 people had the same question and stumbled upon a 9 year old reddit post in less than 24 hours.
